# Overview

This replaces `NESE_FemaleRepeatabilityIsotopes.Rmd`. The question — *do
females tracked more than once keep their individual foraging pattern?* — is
addressed with four complementary analyses:

1. **Strategy fidelity**: do repeat females keep the same strategy more often
   than expected by chance? (permutation test; Cohen's κ)
2. **Behavioural repeatability**: repeatability (R) of the main behavioural
   axes and of interpretable variables, from mixed models with year as a random
   effect (`rptR`).
3. **Spatial fidelity**: is the overlap between two trips of the *same* female
   higher than between trips of *different* females? (randomisation test on
   utilisation distributions)
4. **Isotopic consistency**: population-level repeatability of δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N
   (adjusted for trip type, with year as a random effect), and a comparison of
   within-female isotopic differences with differences between different
   females sampled in the same years.

**What changed from the previous script, and why.** The "individual
repeatability" index (between-individual variance / (between-individual
variance + one seal's residual variance)) is not a defined quantity: per-seal
variances from 2–4 samples are extremely noisy, and conditional residuals from
the mixed model are shrunk towards each seal's mean, pushing the index towards 1.
The previous script also attached those values to the wrong seals (`ddply`
returns seals in alphabetical order, which were then relabelled in data order)
and dropped one female through hard-coded row indices. Isotopes alone also
cannot detect switching between the two offshore strategies, which are
isotopically very similar. Repeatability is therefore estimated here only at
the population level, and fidelity is tested directly on behaviour and space.

**Run first:** `NESE_PB_ForagingStrategies.Rmd`, `NESE_PM_ForagingStrategies.Rmd`
(strategy assignments) and `NESE_SpatialStrategies.Rmd` (individual UDs).

```{r libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(rptR)
library(lme4)
```

# Settings

```{r settings}
SEED <- 20261103
set.seed(SEED)

PCA_DATA    <- "../data/f.PCAdata.1.rds"
META_FILE   <- "../data/IsotopesDatasetForLuis_2023_4_4.csv"   # TOPPID -> MainID
REPEAT_DATA <- "../data/NESE_RepeatData.rds"                   # isotope samples (as in the old script)
PB_ASSIGN   <- "../results/PB_strategies/A_strategy_assignments.csv"
PM_ASSIGN   <- "../results/PM_strategies/A_strategy_assignments.csv"
UD_FILE     <- "../results/spatial_strategies/spatial_UDs.rds"

# Seals excluded from the isotope analysis in the original script
ISO_EXCLUDE <- c("RG180", "RG182", "RG184", "RG185", "RG187", "RG191")

N_PERM      <- 9999   # permutations / randomisations
N_RPT_BOOT  <- 1000   # rptR bootstrap replicates (CIs)
N_RPT_PERM  <- 1000   # rptR permutations (P-values)
MIN_REP_WITHIN <- 5   # minimum repeat females to estimate repeatability within one trip type

OUT <- "../results/female_consistency"
FIG <- "../figures/female_consistency"
dir.create(OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(FIG, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

BEHAV <- c("MaxLat_degrees", "MinLon_degrees", "MedianDistToContShelf_km", "SdDistContShelf_km",
           "MesoEcoProportionShelf", "MesoEcoProportionCAC", "MesoEcoProportionSubArcticPac",
           "MesoEcoProportionNorthCPac", "Mean_Depth_m", "Mean_Depth_sd", "Mean_Duration_sec",
           "Mean_Duration_sd", "Pct_TransitDives", "Pct_ForagingDives", "Pct_DriftDives",
           "Pct_BenthicDives", "PctTripDiving", "DeepDayForageDivesMedian_m",
           "DeepNightForageDivesMedian_m")
ISO <- c("d13C", "d15N")
TRIP_LAB <- c(PostBreeding = "PB", PostMolt = "PM")
```

## Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# Cohen's kappa for two vectors of categorical labels
cohen_kappa <- function(a, b) {
  lev <- union(a, b); a <- factor(a, lev); b <- factor(b, lev)
  tab <- table(a, b); n <- sum(tab)
  po <- sum(diag(tab)) / n; pe <- sum(rowSums(tab) * colSums(tab)) / n^2
  (po - pe) / (1 - pe)
}

# Fit rptR::rpt() without printing its progress bars into the report
fit_rpt <- function(...) {
  out <- NULL
  invisible(capture.output(out <- rpt(...)))
  out
}

# Read one random-effect component (e.g. "MainID") from rptR's printed summary.
# rptR's object layout differs between versions; the printed summary does not.
rpt_parse <- function(r, comp) {
  txt <- capture.output(print(summary(r)))
  i <- grep(paste0("^\\s*", comp, " \\("), txt)[1]
  if (is.na(i)) return(NULL)
  k <- grep("Repeatability estimation overview", txt)
  k <- k[k > i][1]
  if (is.na(k)) return(NULL)
  hdr  <- strsplit(trimws(txt[k + 1]), "\\s+")[[1]]
  vals <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(strsplit(trimws(txt[k + 2]), "\\s+")[[1]]))
  if (length(hdr) != length(vals)) return(NULL)
  setNames(vals, hdr)
}

# One row of results: female repeatability (R, CI, P) and the share of variance due to year
rpt_row <- function(r, label, n_obs, n_ind, n_rep) {
  v  <- if (is.null(r)) NULL else rpt_parse(r, "MainID")
  vy <- if (is.null(r)) NULL else rpt_parse(r, "Year")
  g  <- function(x, nm) if (!is.null(x) && nm %in% names(x)) unname(x[[nm]]) else NA_real_
  if (is.null(v) && !is.null(r)) { message("Could not read R for ", label, "; full output:"); print(summary(r)) }
  data.frame(variable = label, n_obs = n_obs, n_females = n_ind, n_repeat_females = n_rep,
             R = g(v, "R"), SE = g(v, "SE"), lwr = g(v, "2.5%"), upr = g(v, "97.5%"),
             P_LRT = g(v, "LRT_P"), P_permut = g(v, "P_permut"),
             R_year = g(vy, "R"), P_LRT_year = g(vy, "LRT_P"))
}

# Draw one element at random (safe when x has length 1, unlike sample())
pick1 <- function(x) x[sample.int(length(x), 1)]

# All within-female pairs of rows of d (columns: MainID, TOPPID, trip, year, ...)
within_pairs <- function(d) {
  d %>% group_by(MainID) %>% filter(n() > 1) %>%
    group_modify(function(g, key) {
      ij <- t(combn(nrow(g), 2))
      data.frame(TOPPID_1 = g$TOPPID[ij[, 1]], TOPPID_2 = g$TOPPID[ij[, 2]],
                 trip_1 = g$trip[ij[, 1]], trip_2 = g$trip[ij[, 2]],
                 year_1 = g$year[ij[, 1]], year_2 = g$year[ij[, 2]])
    }) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(pair_type = ifelse(trip_1 == trip_2, paste0(trip_1, "-", trip_2), "PB-PM"),
           lag_years = abs(year_2 - year_1))
}
```

# Data

## Tracked trips

```{r tracked}
meta <- read.csv(META_FILE) %>%
  transmute(TOPPID = as.character(TOPPID), MainID = as.character(MainID)) %>%
  distinct(TOPPID, .keep_all = TRUE)

trk <- readRDS(PCA_DATA) %>%
  mutate(TOPPID = as.character(TOPPID)) %>%
  left_join(meta, by = "TOPPID") %>%
  mutate(trip = unname(TRIP_LAB[as.character(Trip)]),
         year = as.integer(as.character(ProcedureYear))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(MainID), !is.na(trip))

# Exclude trips with impossible values (as in the strategy scripts)
pct  <- grep("^Pct", BEHAV, value = TRUE); prop <- grep("^MesoEco", BEHAV, value = TRUE)
bad  <- apply(trk[pct], 1, function(x) any(x < 0 | x > 100)) |
        apply(trk[prop], 1, function(x) any(x < 0 | x > 1))
cat("Excluded trips with impossible values:", paste(trk$TOPPID[bad], collapse = ", "), "\n")
trk <- trk[!bad & complete.cases(trk[BEHAV]), ]

# Strategy assignments
assign <- bind_rows(
  read.csv(PB_ASSIGN) %>% transmute(TOPPID = as.character(TOPPID), trip = "PB", strategy),
  read.csv(PM_ASSIGN) %>% transmute(TOPPID = as.character(TOPPID), trip = "PM", strategy))
trk <- trk %>% left_join(assign, by = c("TOPPID", "trip"))

rep_ids <- trk %>% count(MainID) %>% filter(n > 1) %>% pull(MainID)
cat(nrow(trk), "tracked trips from", n_distinct(trk$MainID), "females;",
    length(rep_ids), "females tracked more than once (",
    sum(trk$MainID %in% rep_ids), "trips)\n")

pairs_trk <- within_pairs(trk %>% dplyr::select(MainID, TOPPID, trip, year))
table(pairs_trk$pair_type)
summary(pairs_trk$lag_years)
```

# 1. Strategy fidelity

For each pair of trips of the same female: did she use the same strategy?
For PB–PM pairs, "same" means the same offshore region (the coastal strategy
has no Post-Moult counterpart, so such pairs count as different). The null
distribution shuffles strategy labels among all trips of the same trip type,
which keeps how common each strategy is.

```{r fidelity}
lab <- setNames(trk$strategy, trk$TOPPID)
fid <- pairs_trk %>%
  mutate(s1 = lab[TOPPID_1], s2 = lab[TOPPID_2]) %>%
  filter(!is.na(s1), !is.na(s2)) %>%
  mutate(same = s1 == s2)
fid %>% dplyr::select(MainID, pair_type, year_1, s1, year_2, s2, same) %>% arrange(pair_type, MainID)

types <- c(sort(unique(fid$pair_type)), "All pairs")
idx_by_trip <- split(seq_len(nrow(trk)), trk$trip)
set.seed(SEED)
null_same <- replicate(N_PERM, {
  s <- trk$strategy
  for (tp in names(idx_by_trip)) { ii <- idx_by_trip[[tp]]; ok <- ii[!is.na(s[ii])]; s[ok] <- sample(s[ok]) }
  sh <- setNames(s, trk$TOPPID)
  same <- sh[fid$TOPPID_1] == sh[fid$TOPPID_2]
  c(tapply(same, fid$pair_type, sum), `All pairs` = sum(same))
})
obs_same <- c(tapply(fid$same, fid$pair_type, sum), `All pairs` = sum(fid$same))
n_pairs  <- c(table(fid$pair_type), `All pairs` = nrow(fid))

fid_tab <- data.frame(pair_type = types, n_pairs = as.vector(n_pairs[types]),
  n_same = as.vector(obs_same[types]),
  expected = rowMeans(null_same)[types],
  P = sapply(types, function(t) (1 + sum(null_same[t, ] >= obs_same[t])) / (N_PERM + 1)),
  row.names = NULL)
fid_tab %>% mutate(across(c(expected, P), ~ signif(.x, 3)))

# Cohen's kappa for pairs of the same trip type (first vs second trip)
kap <- fid %>% filter(pair_type != "PB-PM") %>% group_by(pair_type) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), kappa = if (n() >= 3) cohen_kappa(s1, s2) else NA_real_)
kap
write.csv(fid_tab, file.path(OUT, "1_strategy_fidelity.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(fid, file.path(OUT, "1_strategy_fidelity_pairs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Figure: strategy sequences of repeat females (Fig. 5a)

One row per female tracked more than once. Points are trips, coloured by
strategy (circles = post-breeding, triangles = post-moult); post-moult trips
are drawn half a year after the post-breeding trip of the same year. Solid
lines join consecutive trips with the same strategy, dashed lines a change.
Females that changed strategy are listed at the top.

```{r fig-strategy-sequences, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
STRAT_COLS <- c(Subarctic = "#1b9e77", `North Central Pacific` = "#d95f02",
                `California Current` = "#7570b3")
seq_d <- trk %>%
  filter(MainID %in% rep_ids, !is.na(strategy)) %>%
  mutate(MainID = as.character(MainID),
         x = year + ifelse(trip == "PM", 0.5, 0)) %>%
  arrange(MainID, x)
segs <- seq_d %>% group_by(MainID) %>%
  mutate(xend = dplyr::lead(x), s_next = dplyr::lead(strategy)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(xend)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(change = factor(ifelse(strategy == s_next, "Same strategy", "Changed strategy"),
                         c("Same strategy", "Changed strategy")))
ord <- seq_d %>% group_by(MainID) %>%
  summarise(changed = n_distinct(strategy) > 1, first = min(x)) %>%
  arrange(changed, desc(first)) %>% pull(MainID)          # changers at the top
seq_d$MainID <- factor(seq_d$MainID, ord)
segs$MainID  <- factor(segs$MainID, ord)

all_row <- fid_tab[fid_tab$pair_type == "All pairs", ]
g_seq <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = segs, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = MainID, yend = MainID, linetype = change),
               colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(data = seq_d, aes(x, MainID, fill = strategy, shape = trip), size = 3, stroke = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = STRAT_COLS, name = "Strategy",
                    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21))) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(PB = 21, PM = 24), name = "Trip",
                     labels = c(PB = "Post-breeding", PM = "Post-moult")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`Same strategy` = "solid", `Changed strategy` = "22"),
                        name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(seq_d$year), max(seq_d$year) + 1, 1)) +
  theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey93")) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Female",
       subtitle = sprintf("Same strategy in %d of %d trip pairs (%.1f expected by chance; P = %s)",
                          all_row$n_same, all_row$n_pairs, all_row$expected, signif(all_row$P, 2)))
g_seq
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "1_strategy_sequences.pdf"), g_seq, width = 7, height = 5)
```

# 2. Behavioural repeatability

## A common behavioural space for both trip types

Variables are standardised **within trip type** before the PCA, so the axes
describe how a female differs from other females on the same kind of trip,
rather than the large difference between Post-Breeding and Post-Moult trips.

```{r pca-all}
Z <- trk %>% group_by(trip) %>% mutate(across(all_of(BEHAV), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)))) %>%
  ungroup() %>% dplyr::select(all_of(BEHAV))
pca_all <- prcomp(Z, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
trk$Dim1 <- pca_all$x[, 1]; trk$Dim2 <- pca_all$x[, 2]
# Orient: Dim1 positive = higher latitude; Dim2 positive = longer dives (diving-effort axis)
if (cor(trk$Dim1, trk$MaxLat_degrees) < 0) trk$Dim1 <- -trk$Dim1
if (cor(trk$Dim2, trk$Mean_Duration_sec) < 0) trk$Dim2 <- -trk$Dim2
round(100 * summary(pca_all)$importance[2, 1:4], 1)
ax <- sapply(c("Dim1", "Dim2"), function(d) cor(trk[BEHAV], trk[[d]])[, 1])
lapply(c(Dim1 = "Dim1", Dim2 = "Dim2"), function(d) {
  r <- ax[, d]; round(sort(r[abs(r) >= 0.5], decreasing = TRUE), 2) })
```

## Individual trajectories

Each line joins the trips of one repeat female (points coloured by trip type).
Flat lines = consistent females.

```{r trajectories, fig.height = 5}
traj <- trk %>% filter(MainID %in% rep_ids) %>% arrange(MainID, year)
g <- ggplot(traj, aes(year, Dim1, group = MainID)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_line(colour = "grey40") + geom_point(aes(fill = trip), shape = 21, size = 2.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(PB = "#1b9e77", PM = "#7570b3"), name = "Trip") +
  theme_bw() + labs(x = "Year", y = "Dim 1 score (+ = more northerly / Subarctic)",
                    title = "Repeat females on the main behavioural axis")
g
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "2_trajectories_Dim1.pdf"), g, width = 7, height = 5)

g2 <- trk %>% filter(MainID %in% rep_ids) %>%
  group_by(MainID) %>% mutate(order = rank(year, ties.method = "first")) %>%
  dplyr::select(MainID, order, Dim1) %>% filter(order <= 2) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = order, values_from = Dim1, names_prefix = "trip_") %>%
  ggplot(aes(trip_1, trip_2)) + geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) + coord_equal() + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Dim 1, first trip", y = "Dim 1, second trip")
g2
```

## Repeatability (rptR)

Model: `y ~ Trip + (1 | MainID) + (1 | Year)`. R is the adjusted repeatability
(between-female variance over the sum of the random-effect and residual
variances, with trip type as a fixed effect). All tracked females are used;
females tracked once help estimate the variance components, but the
between-female variance is informed by the repeat females
(`r length(rep_ids)` here), so CIs are wide.

```{r rpt-behaviour}
qlogit <- function(p) { e <- 0.005; qlogis(pmin(pmax(p, e), 1 - e)) }
trk <- trk %>% mutate(MainID = factor(MainID), Year = factor(year), Trip = factor(trip),
                      logit_CAC = qlogit(MesoEcoProportionCAC),
                      log_dist_shelf = log(MedianDistToContShelf_km + 1))
beh_vars <- c(`Dim 1 (latitude / offshore axis)` = "Dim1",
              `Dim 2 (diving-effort axis)` = "Dim2",
              `Maximum latitude` = "MaxLat_degrees",
              `California Current use (logit)` = "logit_CAC",
              `Distance to shelf (log)` = "log_dist_shelf")

set.seed(SEED)
rpt_beh <- bind_rows(lapply(names(beh_vars), function(nm) {
  v <- beh_vars[[nm]]
  r <- fit_rpt(reformulate(c("Trip", "(1 | MainID)", "(1 | Year)"), v),
           grname = c("MainID", "Year"), data = trk, datatype = "Gaussian",
           nboot = N_RPT_BOOT, npermut = N_RPT_PERM)
  rpt_row(r, nm, nrow(trk), nlevels(trk$MainID), length(rep_ids))
}))
rpt_beh %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
write.csv(rpt_beh, file.path(OUT, "2_behaviour_repeatability.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

**Within one trip type.** Estimated only when at least `MIN_REP_WITHIN`
females were tracked twice on that trip type; with fewer, the model cannot
separate within- from between-female variance and R is meaningless (it tends
to 1).

```{r rpt-within-type}
set.seed(SEED)
rpt_within <- bind_rows(lapply(c("PB", "PM"), function(tp) {
  d <- trk %>% filter(trip == tp) %>% droplevels()
  n_rep <- sum(table(d$MainID) > 1)
  if (n_rep < MIN_REP_WITHIN) {
    message("Within ", tp, ": only ", n_rep, " repeat females - repeatability not estimated")
    return(NULL)
  }
  r <- tryCatch(fit_rpt(Dim1 ~ (1 | MainID) + (1 | Year), grname = c("MainID", "Year"), data = d,
                    datatype = "Gaussian", nboot = N_RPT_BOOT, npermut = N_RPT_PERM),
                error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  rpt_row(r, paste("Dim 1, within", tp), nrow(d), nlevels(d$MainID), n_rep)
}))
rpt_within
```

```{r rpt-plot, fig.height = 3.5}
g <- ggplot(rpt_beh, aes(R, reorder(variable, R))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lwr, xmax = upr), width = 0.2, orientation = "y") + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1)) + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Repeatability (R, 95% CI)", y = NULL)
g
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "2_behaviour_repeatability.pdf"), g, width = 7, height = 3.5)
```

# 3. Spatial fidelity

Bhattacharyya's affinity (BA) between the utilisation distributions of two
trips of the same female, compared with BA between trips of different females
of the same pair type. Two nulls:

* **Population null**: the second trip is replaced by a random trip of the same
  type from a different female. Tests whether females return to *their own*
  areas rather than just to the population's area.
* **Strategy null** (same-type pairs only): the replacement trip is drawn from
  the same strategy. Tests fidelity *beyond* strategy membership.

```{r spatial}
if (file.exists(UD_FILE)) {
  ud <- readRDS(UD_FILE)
  P  <- cbind(ud$P_pb, ud$P_pm)
  ud_meta <- bind_rows(ud$seals_pb %>% transmute(TOPPID, trip = "PB", strategy),
                       ud$seals_pm %>% transmute(TOPPID, trip = "PM", strategy)) %>%
    left_join(trk %>% transmute(TOPPID, MainID = as.character(MainID)), by = "TOPPID") %>%
    filter(!is.na(MainID))
  P  <- P[, ud_meta$TOPPID, drop = FALSE]
  BA <- crossprod(sqrt(P))

  sp <- pairs_trk %>% filter(TOPPID_1 %in% ud_meta$TOPPID, TOPPID_2 %in% ud_meta$TOPPID) %>%
    mutate(BA = BA[cbind(TOPPID_1, TOPPID_2)])
  cat(nrow(sp), "within-female trip pairs with UDs\n"); print(table(sp$pair_type))

  # Candidate replacement trips for the second member of each pair
  fem   <- setNames(ud_meta$MainID, ud_meta$TOPPID)
  tripv <- setNames(ud_meta$trip, ud_meta$TOPPID)
  strv  <- setNames(ud_meta$strategy, ud_meta$TOPPID)
  cand_pop <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(sp)), function(k)
    ud_meta$TOPPID[ud_meta$trip == tripv[sp$TOPPID_2[k]] & ud_meta$MainID != sp$MainID[k]])
  cand_str <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(sp)), function(k)
    ud_meta$TOPPID[ud_meta$trip == tripv[sp$TOPPID_2[k]] & ud_meta$MainID != sp$MainID[k] &
                   ud_meta$strategy == strv[sp$TOPPID_2[k]]])

  randomise <- function(cands, rows) {
    set.seed(SEED)
    replicate(N_PERM, {
      j  <- vapply(cands[rows], function(cc) if (length(cc)) pick1(cc) else NA_character_, "")
      ok <- !is.na(j)
      mean(BA[cbind(sp$TOPPID_1[rows][ok], j[ok])])
    })
  }
  sp_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(c(sort(unique(sp$pair_type)), "All pairs"), function(tp) {
    rows <- if (tp == "All pairs") seq_len(nrow(sp)) else which(sp$pair_type == tp)
    obs  <- mean(sp$BA[rows])
    n_pop <- randomise(cand_pop, rows)
    n_str <- if (tp %in% c("PB-PB", "PM-PM")) randomise(cand_str, rows) else NA
    data.frame(pair_type = tp, n_pairs = length(rows), BA_same_female = obs,
               BA_null_population = mean(n_pop), P_population = (1 + sum(n_pop >= obs)) / (N_PERM + 1),
               BA_null_strategy = if (all(is.na(n_str))) NA else mean(n_str),
               P_strategy = if (all(is.na(n_str))) NA else (1 + sum(n_str >= obs)) / (N_PERM + 1))
  }))
  print(sp_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3))))
  write.csv(sp_tab, file.path(OUT, "3_spatial_fidelity.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

  # Figure: BA for same-female pairs vs all different-female pairs of the same type
  ij <- which(upper.tri(BA), arr.ind = TRUE)
  allp <- data.frame(a = colnames(BA)[ij[, 1]], b = colnames(BA)[ij[, 2]], BA = BA[ij]) %>%
    mutate(fa = fem[a], fb = fem[b], ta = tripv[a], tb = tripv[b],
           pair_type = ifelse(ta == tb, paste0(ta, "-", tb), "PB-PM")) %>%
    filter(fa != fb) %>% mutate(which = "Different females")
  g <- ggplot() +
    geom_violin(data = allp, aes(pair_type, BA), fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +
    geom_jitter(data = sp, aes(pair_type, BA), width = 0.08, height = 0, size = 2.2, colour = "#d95f02") +
    theme_bw() + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "UD overlap (Bhattacharyya's affinity)",
         caption = "Grey: pairs of different females; orange: two trips of the same female")
  print(g)
  ggsave(file.path(FIG, "3_spatial_fidelity.pdf"), g, width = 7, height = 4.5)
} else {
  message("Run NESE_SpatialStrategies.Rmd first: ", UD_FILE, " not found.")
}
```

# 4. Isotopic consistency

## Data

The same sample set as the previous script: arrival samples of females, with
the same exclusions.

```{r iso-data}
iso_raw <- if (file.exists(REPEAT_DATA)) readRDS(REPEAT_DATA) else read.csv(META_FILE)
stopifnot(all(c("MainID", "Sex", "TimePeriod", "Trip", "ProcedureYear", ISO) %in% names(iso_raw)))
iso <- iso_raw %>%
  filter(Sex == "Female", TimePeriod == "Arrival", !is.na(d13C), !is.na(d15N),
         !MainID %in% ISO_EXCLUDE) %>%
  transmute(MainID = factor(as.character(MainID)),
            trip = unname(TRIP_LAB[as.character(Trip)]), Trip = factor(trip),
            year = as.integer(as.character(ProcedureYear)), Year = factor(year),
            d13C, d15N) %>%
  filter(!is.na(trip))
iso_rep <- names(which(table(iso$MainID) > 1))
cat(nrow(iso), "samples from", nlevels(iso$MainID), "females;", length(iso_rep),
    "females sampled more than once\n")
table(table(iso$MainID))
```

## Population-level repeatability

Three specifications, from the original to the recommended one:

* (a) **original**: repeat females only, `y ~ Trip + (1 | MainID)`;
* (b) all females, same model;
* (c) **recommended**: all females, `y ~ Trip + (1 | MainID) + (1 | Year)`,
  which removes consistency that is only due to shared isotopic baselines in
  similar years.

```{r rpt-iso}
set.seed(SEED)
rpt_iso <- bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) {
  d_rep <- iso %>% filter(MainID %in% iso_rep) %>% droplevels()
  ra <- fit_rpt(reformulate(c("Trip", "(1 | MainID)"), v), grname = "MainID", data = d_rep,
            datatype = "Gaussian", nboot = N_RPT_BOOT, npermut = N_RPT_PERM)
  rb <- fit_rpt(reformulate(c("Trip", "(1 | MainID)"), v), grname = "MainID", data = iso,
            datatype = "Gaussian", nboot = N_RPT_BOOT, npermut = N_RPT_PERM)
  rc <- fit_rpt(reformulate(c("Trip", "(1 | MainID)", "(1 | Year)"), v), grname = c("MainID", "Year"),
            data = iso, datatype = "Gaussian", nboot = N_RPT_BOOT, npermut = N_RPT_PERM)
  bind_rows(
    rpt_row(ra, paste(v, "(a) repeat females, no year"), nrow(d_rep), nlevels(d_rep$MainID), length(iso_rep)),
    rpt_row(rb, paste(v, "(b) all females, no year"), nrow(iso), nlevels(iso$MainID), length(iso_rep)),
    rpt_row(rc, paste(v, "(c) all females, year random"), nrow(iso), nlevels(iso$MainID), length(iso_rep)))
}))
rpt_iso %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
write.csv(rpt_iso, file.path(OUT, "4_isotope_repeatability.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Model checks for the recommended model
for (v in ISO) {
  m <- lmer(reformulate(c("Trip", "(1 | MainID)", "(1 | Year)"), v), data = iso)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2)); plot(fitted(m), resid(m), main = v, xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residual")
  qqnorm(resid(m), main = v); qqline(resid(m)); par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
}
```

## Within-female differences vs different females in the same years

For every pair of samples from the same female, the absolute isotopic
difference is compared with that between two *different* females sampled in the
same two years and trip types (same baselines). If females are consistent,
their own differences are smaller than these year-matched pairs.

```{r iso-pairs}
iso_pairs <- within_pairs(iso %>% transmute(MainID = as.character(MainID),
                                            TOPPID = paste0(MainID, "_", row_number()),
                                            trip, year))
iso_key <- iso %>% mutate(key = paste0(as.character(MainID), "_", row_number()))
val <- iso_key %>% dplyr::select(key, d13C, d15N)
iso_pairs <- iso_pairs %>%
  mutate(d13C_1 = val$d13C[match(TOPPID_1, val$key)], d13C_2 = val$d13C[match(TOPPID_2, val$key)],
         d15N_1 = val$d15N[match(TOPPID_1, val$key)], d15N_2 = val$d15N[match(TOPPID_2, val$key)],
         abs_d13C = abs(d13C_1 - d13C_2), abs_d15N = abs(d15N_1 - d15N_2))
cat(nrow(iso_pairs), "within-female sample pairs\n")

# Candidate samples from other females with the same year and trip type (fallback: same trip type)
pool <- iso_key %>% transmute(key, MainID = as.character(MainID), trip, year, d13C, d15N)
cands <- function(fem, tp, yr) {
  c1 <- which(pool$MainID != fem & pool$trip == tp & pool$year == yr)
  if (length(c1)) c1 else which(pool$MainID != fem & pool$trip == tp)
}
c1 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(iso_pairs)), function(k) cands(iso_pairs$MainID[k], iso_pairs$trip_1[k], iso_pairs$year_1[k]))
c2 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(iso_pairs)), function(k) cands(iso_pairs$MainID[k], iso_pairs$trip_2[k], iso_pairs$year_2[k]))

set.seed(SEED)
null_iso <- replicate(N_PERM, {
  d <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(iso_pairs)), function(k) {
    a <- pick1(c1[[k]])
    b_c <- c2[[k]][pool$MainID[c2[[k]]] != pool$MainID[a]]
    if (!length(b_c)) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
    b <- pick1(b_c)
    c(abs(pool$d13C[a] - pool$d13C[b]), abs(pool$d15N[a] - pool$d15N[b]))
  }, numeric(2))
  rowMeans(d, na.rm = TRUE)
})
iso_tab <- data.frame(isotope = ISO,
  mean_abs_diff_same_female = c(mean(iso_pairs$abs_d13C), mean(iso_pairs$abs_d15N)),
  mean_abs_diff_year_matched_null = rowMeans(null_iso),
  P = c((1 + sum(null_iso[1, ] <= mean(iso_pairs$abs_d13C))) / (N_PERM + 1),
        (1 + sum(null_iso[2, ] <= mean(iso_pairs$abs_d15N))) / (N_PERM + 1)))
iso_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
write.csv(iso_tab, file.path(OUT, "4_isotope_pair_differences.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Does consistency decline with time between samples?

```{r iso-lag, fig.height = 4}
lag_tests <- sapply(c(d13C = "abs_d13C", d15N = "abs_d15N"), function(v) {
  ct <- cor.test(iso_pairs$lag_years, iso_pairs[[v]], method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
  c(rho = unname(ct$estimate), P = ct$p.value)
})
round(lag_tests, 3)

g <- iso_pairs %>% dplyr::select(lag_years, pair_type, abs_d13C, abs_d15N) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(abs_d13C, abs_d15N), names_to = "isotope", values_to = "diff") %>%
  mutate(isotope = recode(isotope, abs_d13C = "|Δ δ¹³C|", abs_d15N = "|Δ δ¹⁵N|")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(lag_years, diff)) +
  geom_hline(data = data.frame(isotope = c("|Δ δ¹³C|", "|Δ δ¹⁵N|"),
                               y = rowMeans(null_iso)),
             aes(yintercept = y), linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_jitter(aes(shape = pair_type), width = 0.1, height = 0, size = 2.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "black", se = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ isotope, scales = "free_y") + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Years between samples", y = "Absolute difference (‰)", shape = "Pair",
       caption = "Dashed: mean difference between different females in the same years")
g
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "4_isotope_differences_vs_lag.pdf"), g, width = 8, height = 4, device = cairo_pdf)
```

# Suggested Methods text

*We assessed whether females tracked on more than one trip kept their
foraging pattern with four complementary analyses. (1) Strategy fidelity: for
each pair of trips by the same female we recorded whether she used the same
strategy (for post-breeding–post-moult pairs, the same offshore region), and
compared the number of consistent pairs with a null distribution obtained by
permuting strategy labels among trips of the same type (9,999 permutations);
we also report Cohen's κ. (2) Behavioural repeatability: after standardising
behavioural variables within trip type, we summarised them by principal
component analysis and estimated the adjusted repeatability of the first two
components and of maximum latitude, California Current use and distance to the
continental shelf with linear mixed models including trip type as a fixed
effect and female and year as random effects (rptR; Stoffel et al. 2017;
parametric bootstrap CIs and permutation tests). (3) Spatial fidelity: we
compared the overlap (Bhattacharyya's affinity) between utilisation
distributions of two trips of the same female with that obtained when one trip
was replaced by a random trip of the same type from a different female, and, for
pairs of the same trip type, from a different female of the same strategy
(9,999 randomisations). (4) Isotopic consistency: we estimated the adjusted
repeatability of δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N with trip type as a fixed effect and female and
year as random effects, and compared absolute isotopic differences between
samples of the same female with those between different females sampled in the
same years and trip types (9,999 randomisations).*
